transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because ever since my choir friend passed away so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself. I find myself crying over little things, like the potluck lists, and getting all worked up about phone calls I used to handle just fine. I’ve even started missing church planning things, and that’s not like me at all.
How long have you been feeling this way since your friend passed away?
It’s been about a month now, ever since my close friend from choir died.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure I’d call it losing interest. I mean, I still care about those things, but it’s been harder to get myself to go or be involved like I used to.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your friend passed away?
I haven’t really noticed any change in my weight. I don’t think that’s been different.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything or like you're worthless since your friend passed away?
I don’t think so. I mean, I feel sad about him being gone, but I haven’t really been feeling worthless or guilty in that way.
Do you find yourself constantly thinking about your friend who passed away, even when you're doing other things?
I don’t know if I’d say constantly. He does come to mind, sure, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s happening all the time, even when I’m doing other things.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

I wouldn’t say sad every minute of the day, but ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I get teary over little things, like the potluck lists, and things I used to handle fine, like phone calls, get me all worked up now.
Are there things you used to enjoy doing that you no longer find pleasure in?
I’m not really sure. I still do some of the same things, but I guess I haven’t paid close attention to whether I enjoy them the same way. Nothing specific comes to mind right now.
Have you felt less interested in the things you used to enjoy since your friend passed away?
I’m not really sure. I know things feel different since he passed, but I can’t say for sure that I’m less interested in things I used to enjoy. I just haven’t really paid attention to it that way.
Do you feel like you're getting as much pleasure out of the things you're still doing as you used to before your friend passed away?
I’m not sure, honestly. I still do some things, but I haven’t really noticed whether they feel as good as they used to. It’s more that everything’s just felt kind of different since then.
Are there things you used to do that you've stopped doing altogether since your friend passed away?

Yes… I’ve started missing church planning things, and I never used to do that. Since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. Even things like the potluck lists get to me now, and calls I used to handle without thinking feel like too much.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy since your friend passed away?

I don’t really know how to answer that clearly. I’ve stopped showing up for some things like I used to, but I can’t say if it’s because I lost interest or if it just feels harder right now. Everything just feels different since he died.
Do you feel sad most of the day, nearly every day?
I don’t know if I’d say most of the day, nearly every day. I do feel sad, yes, but I haven’t really been keeping track of how much of the day it is. It comes and goes.
For how many days in a row have you been feeling sad since your friend passed away?
It’s been about a month now, since my choir friend died. Not every minute of every day, but the sadness has been there on and off through that whole time.
Do you feel like you're getting less pleasure out of things you're still doing compared to before your friend passed away?
I’m not really sure. Some things don’t feel the same, but I can’t tell if I’m getting less pleasure from them or if I’m just distracted by everything that happened.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss since your friend passed away?
I haven’t really noticed any significant weight loss. I don’t think my weight has changed much, at least not enough that I’ve paid attention to it.
Would you say that feeling sad is something that happens to you almost every day?

Yes, I’d say almost every day. Ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself. I’ll cry over little things, like the potluck lists, and I get all worked up about calls I used to handle just fine.
Do you find yourself preoccupied with thoughts of your friend who passed away to the point where it interferes with your daily activities?
Yes, it does get in the way. I’ve had to let other church members take over some of the calls, the lists, and parts of the luncheon because I’m just not keeping up with it like I always did before.
Have you had intense yearning or longing for your friend since they passed away?
I don’t know if I’d call it intense yearning. I do miss her, and I think about her, but I’m not sure it’s that kind of longing you mean.
Have you had intense longing for your friend who passed away?
I’m not really sure I’d call it intense longing. I miss her, of course, but I don’t know if it’s that strong kind of feeling you mean.
